## Success Patterns

### SP-002: Iterative Visual Feedback Refinement
**Category:** Execution  
**Success Rate:** 100% (5/5 iterations)  
**Key:** canvas  
**Pattern ID:** iterative-visual-feedback

**Pattern Description:**
Incremental CSS layout improvements driven by user-provided screenshots, using checkpoint commits for safety and progressive enhancement.

**Implementation Workflow:**
1. Checkpoint commit (establish rollback point)
2. Initial implementation (interpret requirements)
3. Screenshot validation (user feedback)
4. Refinement (targeted changes, not rewrites)
5. Build validation (ensure zero errors/warnings)
6. Commit + document (record progress)
7. Iterate (repeat 3-6 until complete)

**Success Indicators:**
- Clean builds maintained (0 errors, 0 warnings)
- Average iteration time: ~3 minutes
- Solution found in 2-3 iterations
- No CSS regressions introduced
- Consistent debug markers applied

**Code Example:**
```css
/* Success Pattern: Auto-expanding with equal heights */
.grid-container { 
  display: grid; 
  align-items: stretch; /* Forces equal heights */
  height: auto; /* Expands based on content */
}
.grid-child { 
  height: 100%; /* Fills grid cell */
  overflow-y: auto; /* Internal scrolling */
}
```

**Learned From:** canvas key (commits: 6902ad9, 5be8797, a6927a3, a202065, 9869cfd)

**When to Apply:**
- UI layout requirements unclear initially
- Visual requirements evolving through feedback
- CSS Grid or Flexbox layout challenges

### SP-005: SignalR Hub Method Validation
**Category:** Error Handling  
**Success Rate:** 100% (after fix)  
**Key:** canvas  
**Pattern ID:** signalr-hub-validation

**Pattern Description:**
Always validate that SignalR hub methods exist before invoking them from client code, preventing HubException crashes.

**Anti-Pattern:**
```csharp
// ❌ Invoking non-existent hub method
await hubConnection.InvokeAsync("NotifyQuestionDeleted", questionId);
// Result: HubException: Method does not exist → Blazor circuit disconnect
```

**Success Pattern:**
```csharp
// ✅ UI-only operation (no SignalR)
questions.RemoveAll(q => q.QuestionId == questionId);
StateHasChanged();

// ✅ OR proper hub method invocation (when method exists)
await hubConnection.InvokeAsync("DeleteQuestion", questionId);
```

**Success Indicators:**
- Zero `HubException: Method does not exist` errors
- Blazor circuits remain stable
- Clear separation between UI-only and broadcast operations
- Comprehensive E2E test coverage

**Learned From:** canvas key (signalr-error-fixes, questionid-type-fix phases)

### SP-006: GUID vs Int Type Mismatch Resolution
**Category:** Error Handling  
**Success Rate:** 100% (after fix)  
**Key:** canvas  
**Pattern ID:** guid-type-mismatch-fix

**Pattern Description:**
When API returns GUID strings but frontend treats them as integers, systematically update all type references.

**Root Cause:**
- API returns: `"038893e4-4476-4e23-aff4-0cfa79e54b9d"` (GUID string)
- Frontend model: `public int QuestionId { get; set; }` (integer)
- Result: 404 errors on API endpoints, comparison failures

**Solution Workflow:**
1. API contract review (verify actual response types)
2. Frontend model update (`int` → `string`)
3. Handler updates (all event handlers receiving GUIDs)
4. Comparison logic (replace integer comparisons)
5. Remove workarounds (delete `GetHashCode()` hacks)
6. E2E validation (comprehensive test)

**Code Fix:**
```csharp
// Before: Type mismatch
public class QuestionData { public int QuestionId { get; set; } }
questions.FirstOrDefault(q => q.QuestionId == response.QuestionId.GetHashCode());

// After: Correct types
public class QuestionData { public string QuestionId { get; set; } }
questions.FirstOrDefault(q => q.QuestionId == response.QuestionId);
```

**Learned From:** canvas key (questionid-type-fix-and-e2e-test phase)

### SP-007: Unified Service Wrapper Pattern
**Category:** Optimization  
**Success Rate:** 100%  
**Key:** hcp  
**Pattern ID:** unified-service-wrapper

**Pattern Description:**
Create unified service wrapper providing mode-based functionality (Host vs Participant) while maintaining backward compatibility.

**Code Example:**
```csharp
public class UnifiedHtmlTransformService {
    private readonly HtmlParsingService _parser;
    private readonly AssetProcessingService _assetProcessor;
    
    // Host mode: Core transformation + share buttons
    public async Task<string> TransformForHostAsync(string html, long sessionId) {
        var transformed = _parser.TransformHtml(html);
        return await _assetProcessor.InjectAssetShareButtonsAsync(
            transformed, sessionId.ToString());
    }
    
    // Participant mode: Core transformation only
    public string TransformForParticipant(string html) {
        return _parser.TransformHtml(html);
    }
}
```

**Success Indicators:**
- Single source of truth for common operations
- Consistent validation and error handling
- No breaking changes (backward compatible)
- Clear mode separation

**Learned From:** hcp key (unified HTML transformation service)

**When to Apply:**
- Multiple services with overlapping responsibilities
- Different modes requiring different feature sets
- Need for centralized validation/error handling

### SP-004: Dual-Pattern Regex for Production HTML
**Category:** Error Handling  
**Success Rate:** 100% (8/8 test cases)  
**Key:** hcp  
**Pattern ID:** dual-pattern-regex

**Pattern Description:**
When HTML structure varies between environments, implement multiple regex patterns to handle all variations.

**Code Example:**
```csharp
// Pattern 1: Production HTML with <span> tags
var pattern1 = @"<span[^>]*>(\s*-\s*[^<]+?)</span>";
html = Regex.Replace(html, pattern1, "", RegexOptions.IgnoreCase);

// Pattern 2: Legacy HTML with plain text
var pattern2 = @"(<h4[^>]*>[^<]*<i[^>]*></i>\s*)([^<]+?)(\s-\s[A-Za-z,\s]+)(</h4>)";
html = Regex.Replace(html, pattern2, "$1$2$4", RegexOptions.IgnoreCase);

// Metrics
Logger.LogInformation($"Bytes removed: pattern1={bytes1}, pattern2={bytes2}");
```

**Success Indicators:**
- Handles all HTML variations (dev, staging, production)
- Zero false positives/negatives
- Performance acceptable (<100ms)
- Comprehensive test coverage

**Learned From:** hcp key (hadees token removal, plain text button removal)

### SP-003: Archive-Before-Delete Safety Protocol
**Category:** Execution  
**Success Rate:** 100% (16/16 keys archived safely)  
**Key:** system  
**Pattern ID:** archive-before-delete

**Pattern Description:**
Always move files/folders to archive before permanent deletion, preserving history and enabling recovery.

**Workflow:**
1. Identify obsolete items (no work logs, old activity)
2. Create archive structure (`_archived/` with date prefix)
3. Move (don't delete) to archive
4. Document archive (update tracking files)
5. Validate no active references
6. Periodic review (quarterly for permanent deletion)

**Success Indicators:**
- Zero data loss
- Recovery capability maintained
- Audit trail preserved
- Active workspace footprint reduced

**Learned From:** system key (16 keys archived 2025-10-10)

### MP-003: Type Mismatch Patterns Repeat Across Features
**Trend:** CONCERNING  
**Evidence:** GUID vs int mismatch in canvas, similar patterns elsewhere  

**Insight:**
Type mismatches recur because:
- No compile-time contract validation (C# backend, TypeScript frontend)
- Manual synchronization between DTOs and models
- Inconsistent API response types
- Insufficient E2E testing

**Recommendation:** Implement API contract validation, generate TypeScript types from C# DTOs
